• It was officially completed in 2012.

So, the tallest self‐supporting tower was completed in 2012.

The tallest self‐supporting tower is the CN Tower in Toronto, Canada, which was completed in 1976.

While the Eiffel Tower (completed in 1889) is famous for being a self‐supporting lattice tower, it is shorter than the CN Tower. The CN Tower, built as a communications and observation tower, held the record as the tallest free‐standing structure in the world until later structures like the Burj Khalifa were built (though the Burj Khalifa is supported by a buttressed core rather than being “free‐standing” in the same sense). 

So, the answer is: 1976.
